Title: Inspection of an Energy Drink Bottling Machine

You develop an application that helps you with the inspection of a machine.
After entering the type of the machine, and its serial number, the inspection can begin:

The description says inspection begins after entering required identifiers, actions collect or enter values, and additional questions depend on results.

result.rule: Follow the BPMN XML schema: never put a documentation element directly inside bpmn:definitions, and never nest a sequenceFlow inside a task, gateway or event. If you add an ioSpecification, it must contain its dataInput and dataOutput elements first, then at least one inputSet and one outputSet, even if empty: <bpmn:inputSet/><bpmn:outputSet/>.
Use bpmn:sequenceFlow for execution order between flow nodes in the same process or subprocess scope; set valid sourceRef and targetRef values.
Several unconditional outgoing flows from one activity can all proceed. Use a gateway when the description requires a decision or synchronization.

Give every process and every expanded subProcess its own explicit start event and end event. A trigger that occurs after the main flow (for example later feedback or a return) is joined to the main flow by a gateway, or modeled as an event subprocess or a separate process.
Verify processRef values, lane membership, message-flow endpoints and directions, and the prohibition on sequence flows between pools.
Do not merge separately described actions into one task or split one stated action without a process reason. Preserve described dependencies.

When the description states that activities have an order or repetition, or that work happens concurrently: Model the stated order and repetition with sequence flows and loops, and model concurrent work with appropriate gateways, preserving the described dependencies.

When the description states distinct participant actions and their order, or describes outcomes that determine subsequent paths: Model each stated action as a corresponding BPMN activity, connect activities in the stated order, and represent outcome-dependent paths with appropriate gateways and flows.

When the description states that a downstream activity can begin only after multiple prerequisite activities are complete: join the prerequisite paths with a parallel gateway, then connect that gateway to the dependent activity with a sequence flow

args.text: When the description distinguishes activities by who acts and how values are obtained—for example, a person inputs answers versus machine values being collected automatically—use labels that preserve those described actions and do not substitute a different activity.

trace.reason: Check whether existing documented guidance already covers faithful activity labeling and how the instruction relates to it.

result.rule: Use short, faithful labels in the input language. Prefer verb-object activity names and meaningful business triggers or outcomes for events.
Model every distinct activity, event, participant, decision, branch, loop, message and outcome stated in the description. Do not invent process facts.
Do not infer a task subtype only from a verb in its label; require supporting meaning in the full description.
Do not merge separately described actions into one task or split one stated action without a process reason. Preserve described dependencies.
Distinguish message tasks from message events: a task models performed work; an event models a message occurrence affecting flow.
Use transaction, ad-hoc or compensation behavior only when its specific semantics are explicitly described.

args.text: When a process description distinguishes activities or decisions by their stated action, input, or outcome, preserve that meaning in BPMN labels rather than substituting a different action or question.

result.rule: When the description states a specific activity, decision, or outcome: Label the corresponding BPMN element with wording that preserves the described action and its object or result; do not substitute a related but different action or outcome.

When the description names an activity or outcome with multiple stated actions, alternatives, or a distinguishing object or participant.: Label the corresponding BPMN activity or event so its described scope remains identifiable. Preserve materially stated actions, alternatives, and objects or participants; do not substitute a broader or different action or add unsupported details.

When the description states a specific business trigger or process outcome for a start or end event: Label the corresponding BPMN event with a concise phrase that preserves that stated trigger or outcome, rather than using a generic label such as “start” or “end”.

When the description distinguishes different actions or process states involving the same participant or subject at different stages: Label each BPMN activity and outcome to reflect the specific action or state described at that stage; do not substitute a different action or an unsupported outcome.
